symptom: On a clean database, MakeUsersUsernameNullable executes before the migration that creates users.

evidence.primary_error: Migration MakeUsersUsernameNullable20260831095333 failed because users does not exist.
evidence.framework_behavior: TypeORM 0.3.27 parses only the last 13 characters of each migration name and sorts numerically.
evidence.incorrect_order: The 14-digit 2026... suffixes became 260... timestamps and sorted before 1700000000000 and 1788495106545.

root_cause.summary: Five migration classes used 14-digit calendar strings instead of 13-digit JavaScript timestamps. TypeORM does not use filenames as the ordering authority.

actions_attempted: Renamed the five affected migration files and class suffixes to unique sequential 13-digit timestamps 1788495106546 through 1788495106550.
Compared every renamed source with its HEAD predecessor and confirmed all up/down operations are unchanged.
Ran targeted migration ESLint, a clean temporary TypeScript compile, and the Nest production build.
Attempted Docker CLI discovery without deleting or resetting a volume.
resolution: Source correction is complete and deterministic ordering is verified; Docker runtime confirmation is blocked by the unavailable CLI.
reusable_resolution: Migration class names must end in unique 13-digit JavaScript timestamps; filename order alone is not sufficient.
prevention: Reject migration class suffixes that are not exactly 13 digits and inspect the TypeORM-derived numeric order before Docker startup.
